I have been doing wheat-maize on this land for many years. My son works in the city, so it is just me on 16.1 mu, but I rent the machine for plowing and harvest, so I can manage. I will do what I did last year because the harvest was decent — about 550 kg wheat and 600 kg maize per mu.

For wheat, I plant in October. I use the improved variety the seed shop sells — Jimai or whatever they have, the dealer in town tells me what is good that year. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) before plowing, about 50 kg per mu, that is one bag. Then I topdress with urea around returning-green time, maybe 25-30 kg per mu. So altogether nitrogen comes to about 20 kg per mu pure N, phosphorus and potassium each around 7-8 kg per mu. I would rather put a little extra than have yellow leaves later. I plow with rotary tiller, it is faster.

Irrigation for wheat — I water before winter, then at returning-green, jointing, and grain filling. Four times. The well is mine to use. I spray for weeds in spring once, and for aphids and powdery mildew once or twice depending on the year.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I do no-till — just plant straight into the wheat stubble, less work and the straw protects the soil. Hybrid maize seed of course, Zhengdan or Xianyu type. I use compound fertilizer at planting and urea at big-trumpet stage. Total nitrogen maybe 22 kg per mu. Maize needs more N than wheat I think. Irrigation 2-3 times if the summer rain is not enough. Spray for armyworm and corn borer.
